newsitem.title: USA: Chiron sees Myotrophin, DepoCyt approval.
newsitem.headline: Chiron sees Myotrophin, DepoCyt approval.

text.p: Chiron Corp expects the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to approve its Myotrophin and DepoCyt products next year, President and Chief Executive Officer Edward Penhoet said on Tuesday.
Myotrophin, jointly developed by Chiron and Cephalon Inc as a treatment fo Lou Gehrig's disease, was recommended last year by an FDA advisory panel.
DepoCyt, an injectable treatment for neoplastic meningitis, is currently in Phase 4 trials.

Speaking at the Hambrecht and Quist Healthcare Conference in San Francisco, Penhoet said he expected the growing use of a three-drug "cocktail" to treat AIDS patients would further increase the use of Chiron's bDNA probe tests.

The bDNA probe test measures AIDS viral load -- a key measure of the effectiveness of the three-drug therapy, which has been successful in diminishing the symptoms and staying the progression of AIDS.
